assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is among the most widely used bond constructions in synthesis, from medicinal chemistry to materials; it is a clear, general methodology advance with enormous practical reach, squarely within the efficiency-and-generality ethos of synthetic methodology.
assessment.attribution: The decisive ligand-controlled, general amination methods came from the Buchwald and Hartwig groups, with the earlier tin-amide precedent credited to Kosugi; the two independent, parallel developers form a natural two-person configuration. The Kosugi precedent is a minor allocation wrinkle.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, industrial-scale use and stable mechanistic understanding; recognition is, if anything, overdue, and the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 Nobel for cross-coupling is judged to already cover this area; the weight of Kosugi's earlier contribution relative to the two principal laureates cannot be verified from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced protein degradation, via bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, created a new therapeutic modality and revealed the mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs; the conceptual originality is high and the chemistry is genuinely molecular design.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others made major later contributions, so a three-person cap forces hard choices on credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in trials with approvals still pending, but target engagement mechanism and generality are well confirmed across many labs; timing is reasonable and arguably close to ripe.
uncertainties: Crowded credit across several groups; clinical validation is incomplete; the split between the PROTAC and molecular glue strands is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs for site-specific incorporation of nonnatural amino acids re-engineered the genetic code and gave chemists direct control over protein composition; the idea is original and the methodology is broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and co-workers launched the field, with Wang as lead experimentalist of the first systems; Chin extended it to multiple codons, orthogonal ribosomes and whole-organism use. Mehl and Yokoyama are real contributors, so the three-person limit leaves some credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of reproduction in many laboratories, with stable interpretation and widespread use in chemical biology and therapeutics discovery; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether recognition is better framed as chemistry rather than biology; allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert one base into another without double-strand cleavage by evolving deaminase fusions; this is chemical thinking applied to the genome, with immediate therapeutic implications and high originality.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual design and directed evolution; Komor made the first cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor as lead investigators. Related independent work by Nishida and Kondo is credited but is a somewhat different, parallel design.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and first clinical results are encouraging, but long-term clinical safety and off-target profiles are still maturing; the 2020 CRISPR prize may make a close follow-on feel less urgent.
uncertainties: Premature versus timely given clinical data are still emerging; relationship to the existing CRISPR prize; role of Nishida and Kondo.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalyst-controlled C-H functionalization lets chemists treat C-H bonds as functional groups and rework synthetic planning, with ligand-enabled and directing-group strategies offering real step economy; this speaks directly to efficiency in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu pioneered ligand-accelerated and template-controlled distal selectivity; Sanford and Hartwig made foundational contributions in Pd-catalysed and Ir-catalysed borylation chemistry respectively. The field is wide, so a narrow trio will leave out other pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Broadly applied in late-stage functionalization and increasingly in industry; selectivity is not yet predictable for arbitrary substrates, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Fragmented credit across many pioneering strands; Hartwig also appears in a competing entry; the field may be seen as not yet fully mature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a vast array of radical reactions under mild conditions and has transformed discovery-scale synthesis; breadth and adoption are impressive.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 to 2009 reports from Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz (alongside MacMillan, who is already a laureate) are the decisive ones, though Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre contributed significantly. Credit is tangled, and MacMillan's existing laureate status complicates a configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used in industry; mechanistic understanding is mature, but the novelty of the catalytic concept relative to earlier photochemistry may be challenged.
uncertainties: MacMillan's prior Nobel for organocatalysis and his role here; priority questions relative to earlier photochemistry work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized mesoporous TiO2 solar cell introduced a molecularly engineered photovoltaic and sparked a large field of molecular photochemistry and energy materials, including the lineage to perovskite cells; the 1991 paper is a landmark.
assessment.attribution: Grätzel is the clear intellectual leader and O'Regan the first author of the foundational paper. Hagfeldt is a major later contributor but not decisive to the founding discovery.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation, but the technology has had limited commercial success and its legacy is partly overtaken by perovskites; recognition is timely in scientific impact, though practical impact is debated.
uncertainties: Modest commercial success; possible preference for the perovskite entry; role of O'Regan versus Hagfeldt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments and brought total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins within reach; a real synthetic chemistry achievement with broad use.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 method came from Kent, Dawson and Muir with co-workers; Kent is the principal driver. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu represent extensions and alternatives, so inclusion will leave some deserving colleagues out.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation, stable interpretation and routine use for protein engineering; the impact on mainstream chemistry is clear, though somewhat narrower than that of the leading entries.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact relative to other chemical biology entries; allocation among Kent, Dawson, Muir and Danishefsky.
